Network Security

Automated Indicator Sharing

The automatic exchange of cyber threat indicators between organizations and trusted partners using standardized formats (e.g., STIX/TAXII) as specified in NIST SP 800-150 and DHS AIS.

Quick answer: The automatic exchange of cyber threat indicators between organizations and trusted partners using standardized formats (e.g., STIX/TAXII) as specified in NIST SP 800-150 and DHS AIS.

Questions and answers

What is Automated Indicator Sharing?

In this glossary, Automated Indicator Sharing refers to: The automatic exchange of cyber threat indicators between organizations and trusted partners using standardized formats (e.g., STIX/TAXII) as specified in NIST SP 800-150 and DHS AIS.

How is Automated Indicator Sharing used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Our SOC participates in automated indicator sharing to receive and distribute real-time threat intelligence with trusted partners."

Automated Indicator Sharing matters because it supports clear communication in Network Security contexts for SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, and CEH.
